narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 52% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. This is only slightly above the threshold, so the decision is not a certainty but reflects a balance of risk factors leaning against approval.

The strongest factor in your file was your savings balance of at least 1,000 DM. This worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward good credit, even though such a high savings level is uncommon among approved applicants. However, two other factors outweighed that strength. The second most influential factor was the loan purpose: a new car. Compared with approved applicants, new-car loans are less common than borrowing for radio/TV or furniture/equipment, and this factor pushed toward bad credit. The third factor was your checking-account status of 0–200 DM, which also pushed toward bad credit, suggesting a limited account buffer; only 18.4% of approved applicants had this status.

To improve your next application, focus on strengthening your checking-account balance and maintaining it over time. Consider reducing the requested amount or delaying a new-car purchase, and ask the bank whether a smaller loan, a different purpose, or adding a suitable guarantor or co-applicant would help. Providing updated savings and account records after a few months of stable balances would also make your profile more convincing.
